finding.title: Add UNIQUE(profileId, ulid) to PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions — sync merge can double-credit a child's points
finding.rule: DB-6 (sync-able entity integrity) / profileId-in-PK's composite-index companion requirement
finding.why: PointsLedger and RewardRedemptions both carry a `ulid` column documented as "cross-device id for append-only cloud sync" — the exact same purpose LearningLedger's `ulid` serves, where it is protected by a real `UNIQUE(profileId, ulid)` @TableIndex. Neither PointsLedger nor RewardRedemptions has any uniqueKeys/@TableIndex at all. PointsLedgerMerger's own comment says entries are "deduplicated on ulid via INSERT-OR-IGNORE," but points_balance_dao.dart's insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent actually does a manual SELECT-then-INSERT with no DB constraint backing it — a classic TOCTOU race. If two merge calls for the same ulid ever interleave (concurrent pulls, a retried tutored pull, a future refactor that parallelizes merges), a duplicate row lands; reDeriveBalanceFromLedger sums ALL ledger deltas, so the child's points balance silently becomes wrong — violating the table's own documented invariant that balance is "the authoritative denormalised sum of all ledger entries."
finding.recommendation: Add `@TableIndex(name: 'points_ledger_profile_ulid', columns: {#profileId, #ulid}, unique: true)` to PointsLedger and an equivalent unique index to RewardRedemptions (mirroring learning_ledger.dart), ship as a schema migration, and switch insertRemoteLedgerEntryIfAbsent to rely on that constraint (insertOnConflictDoNothing) instead of a separate SELECT.
acceptance_criteria: Schema migration adds the unique index to points_ledger and reward_redemptions, with committed schema export + generated migration test (DB-4).
Regression test: calling the merge path twice concurrently (Future.wait) with the same ulid results in exactly one row and exactly one balance credit.
